thesis: Serendib Efreet offered blue a three-mana 3/4 flyer in exchange for one damage each upkeep, importing black’s life-for-rate philosophy into tempo and control decks.

competitiveTimeline.significance: From early Type I and Old School through its famous Revised misprint, Serendib Efreet became both a competitive rate benchmark and one of Magic’s best-known printing anomalies.

playbook.role: Use the Efreet when its four-turn aerial clock outweighs the self-damage, and pair it with disruption that prevents the opponent from racing or answering it efficiently.
